exclude: Generated sprite-mirror cache retained in the loaded file; native mirror routines rebuild these working bytes

comments.text: Enter with native ending files H/I loaded. Set port $35 and stage index five, run shared setup and mirror/attribute initialization, set actor positions and facing, and start music cue four. Each loop waits through $A74F, ticks music, updates sprite coordinates through $9910 and the four-component ending stream through $3490, then refreshes ordering/mirrors. Once $0644 is negative, accumulate $50 in $068F and step player X left on carry; keep the second X 24 units ahead. At X zero, mute SID volume and return.

Decrement $065E when nonzero. On zero, reset it to seven and index four parallel sprite-component streams with $065F, storing their bytes in $6C–$6F and incrementing the index. A zero in the first stream changes phase: initially set $0644=$74 and restart index twelve; later increment $0644 until it turns negative, subtract twelve from player X at that transition, and use index eighteen for the leaving sequence. The shared outer loop interprets the negative phase as walking left.

Twenty-three first-component frame numbers, read by $34A1 with index $065F. A zero is a phase delimiter for $3490 rather than a sprite pointer. Nonzero bytes select shapes in the ending's active VIC-bank-$4000 sprite allocation.
Twenty-three second-component frame numbers read in parallel with the first stream by $34A6–$34AB and stored at $6D. The first stream, not this one, supplies phase termination.
Twenty-three indexed third-component frame numbers plus one retained zero byte, read at $34AD and stored at $6E. It shares the first stream's phase boundaries.
Twenty-three fourth-component frame numbers, read at $34B2 and stored at $6F. It shares the first stream's phase boundaries.

Retained bytes of the original tape-loading template following the ending's four component streams. The ending entry and loop use $3400–$3544; its loaded second page also carries this template fragment. The EasyFlash edition performs its active file loads through the previously installed $020D copy instead.

Ending sprite components and retained graphics from file H, source component 0, visible in VIC bank $4000 as sprite $A3. The first 63 bytes are 24-by-21 hires bits or 12-by-21 two-bit pixels (the VIC mode decides); the 64th byte is alignment padding. The playfield sprite writer at $AD10–$AD15 reads frame pointers from $6A,X and stores them in both screen sprite-pointer tables. Horizontal reflection uses the routines beginning at $FD42. This label identifies a stored shape; its fighting pose is not named.
